To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
number–space synaesthets have a horizontal number line that differs in its ordinality (left-to-right vs. right-to-left) and direction (ascending vs. descending) from that of controls.
the parietal regions are involved in the processing of numbers in synaesthetics.
number-space synaesthetics (MkM and other participants) show a numerical distance effect in the parietal regions, even when the task is not numerical.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of synaesthesia and its relation to other cognitive processes.
the study of the cognitive mechanisms underlying numerical-spatial association and the neural correlates of this phenomenon in synaesthesia.
the study of the neural mechanisms of numerical cognition.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
number-space synaesthesia is not the same as the mental number line, and that number-space synasthetes do not have a mental number line.

the parietal regions of the brain, especially the intraparietalsulcus (IPS) and the supramarginal gyri are involved in automatic numerical-spatial association, and this is true both for synaesthetics and non-synaesthetics.
the parietal lobe is the most probable location for the neural correlates of automatic numerical-spatial associations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
number-space association is not a mere consequence of a spatial representation of numbers.
we have found a strong association between the neural correlates of the mental number line and the spatial representation of numbers in synaesthetics.
the neural mechanisms of number-space association are shared by both synaesthetics and nonsynesthetes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, even when numbers are task‐irlevant, number‐space synesthesia elicits parietal activity.
the parietal regions involved in number processing in nonsynaesthetics are also activated in the synaesthetically experienced MNL.

we have shown that the neural correlates associated to the numerical‐spatial representation are shared by synesthetes and non-synaesthetes, suggesting that the neural mechanisms underlying this representation are similar.
